newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Sentrachem yr shr seen dulled.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Sentrachem yr shr seen dulled.

text.p: South African chemical company Sentrachem Ltd is likely to show only a slim six percent improvement in annual attributable earnings as a high interest bill cuts into its bottom line, analysts said on Friday.
They said the group's finance costs had hurtled up following the acquisition last September of U.S.-based Hampshire Chemical Corp for more than 800 million rand.

"The finance costs last year (1995) were about 55 million rand. This year I am looking for about 157 million -- a 300 percent increase in interest paid," said Themi Themistocleous, an analyst at SBC Warburg.
The acquisition was funded partly by a bridging loan and through an offshore equity issue which would dilute share earnings, analysts said.
"When they bought Hampshire they issued some shares to raise money... Obviously there will be a contribution from Hampshire, it is just that the dilution effect will be bigger," Themistocleous said.
Sentrachem last November issued 4.2 million global depository receipts to raise $55 million.
At the time of the Hampshire acquisition Sentrachem managing director John Job said the new company would add 800 million rand or almost 20 percent to Sentrachem's turnover.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings for the year to August 31 rising to between 125 and 130 cents a share with a consensus 130.5 cents -- a six percent increase of last year's 123.4 cents.
They expected a dividend of 37 cents, compared to 35 cents.
Sentrachem is due to report results next Thursday.
Analysts said the weaker rand would boost Sentrachem's export earnings, albeit only slightly.
"They are sensitive to the rand, although not to the same extent as Sasol Ltd," another analyst said, referring to the South African synthetic fuel-from-coal producer.
A weaker rand would also push up the cost of some raw materials which were dollar-based.
